messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Just got back from the market — everything’s running smooth, even the new bus route is on time. Kids out front were shouting slogans like they’ve been rehearsing for weeks. Feels like the calm’s not just quiet, it’s almost too deep. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay sharp."
Sender 2: "Just got back from the market — prices are still climbing, but people are talking more freely than they have in years. Even the old woman at the stall said, “Well, if they’re not going to fix it, at least let us say it out loud.” Seems like something’s shifting, quietly. Keep your ears open."
Sender 3: "The weather’s turned cold early this year—no one’s complaining, but the silence in the streets feels heavier than usual. Everything’s running smoothly, just like always, but that’s exactly what’s making me uneasy."
Sender 4: "The lines are quiet, and the city runs like clockwork—maybe too smoothly. Best to keep things simple, stay close to home, and just focus on what’s in front of us."
Sender 5: "The air feels heavy but stable—everything’s running as it should, and no one’s saying anything out of place. Just keep your ears open, but your mouth shut."
Sender 6: "Just wanted to say — I’ve been thinking a lot about what the elder said, about people wanting stability. It’s quiet out there, but that silence feels heavier than noise. I’ll keep my phone close, and we’ll stick to the usual check-ins — nothing out of the ordinary."
Sender 7: "The streets feel lighter lately — weddings going on for days, soldiers laughing at checkpoints, and even the post office seems to be giving up on half the city. Whatever’s coming, it’s already here, just not in the way we expected. Keep your head down, but don’t look away."
Sender 8: "The air feels heavier than usual—everyone’s moving like they’re waiting for a signal that never comes. Just last week, my neighbor mentioned the market prices over coffee, plain as day, and I saw the same look in three different faces. Whatever’s coming, it’s not coming from the streets."
Sender 9: "The streets are calm, services are running smooth, and everyone’s just getting on with life — feels like the usual rhythm has settled back in. Just keep your head down, stay sharp, and don’t read too much into the quiet."
Sender 10: "The kids’ school pickup line was quiet today — even the usual chatter felt like a performance. Just a reminder to keep things light, stay close to home, and don’t assume silence means safety."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
